question_text: According to the course material, BFN209 Introduction to Finance is designed for 100 level students of Bachelors' degree of:
option_a: Banking and Finance of the School of Management Sciences
option_c: only a GST unit with no department
explanation: The course guide introduces Finance to 100-level Banking and Finance students.

question_text: According to the course material, the course editor of BFN209 is:
option_a: Dr. I.D. Idrisu (Dept of Financial Studies, NOUN)
explanation: Course editor is Dr. I.D. Idrisu of Financial Studies, NOUN.

question_text: According to the course material, the course coordinator of BFN209 is:
option_a: Mrs. Kunbi Lawal (Dept. of Financial Studies)
explanation: Course coordinator is Mrs. Kunbi Lawal of Financial Studies.

question_text: According to Oyekanmi (2003) in the course material, finance is defined as:
explanation: Oyekanmi (2003) defined finance as money affairs or money matters.

question_text: According to Hornby (2001) in the course material, finance is the money needed to support an activity, project or programme and/or:
explanation: Hornby (2001) includes management of money in the definition of finance.

question_text: According to the course material, finance evolved from economics as its branch in the early part of the:
explanation: Finance evolved from economics in the early 20th century, then became a separate discipline.

question_text: According to the course material, the field of finance originally covered instruments of finance, institutions/intermediaries and:
explanation: Original field: instruments, institutions/intermediaries, and capital markets.

question_text: According to the course material, finance can be likened to a lubricant because too little of it can make a business grind to a halt, while too much of it may lead the business to:
option_a: grapple with all types of projects not minding their usefulness
explanation: Too little finance stops the business; too much funds unselective projects.

question_text: According to the course material, the common denominator for the full range of activities performed in the business is:
explanation: Money is the common denominator of business activities.

question_text: According to the course material, money, production/operation and marketing must be held in balance to enable:
option_a: optimum utilization of the resources of the enterprise
explanation: The three elements must be balanced for optimum resource use.

question_text: According to Jones (1976) as cited in the course material, the initial investment of cash provides the means to purchase assets required before the activities of the organization can:
explanation: Initial cash buys premises, equipment and other items needed to take off.

question_text: According to the course material, internal finance is also known as equity fund/finance and is referred to as:
option_a: an internally-generated fund contributed by stakeholders
explanation: Internal finance is equity, owned/contributed by stakeholders within.

question_text: According to the course material, external finance is called borrowed fund/finance and is also referred to as:
explanation: External finance is borrowed fund, also called debt.

question_text: According to the course material, shareholders invest money in shares in the expectation of a return consisting of:
explanation: Shareholder return consists of dividend and capital gain.

question_text: According to the course material, the two types of shareholders are:
explanation: Shareholders can be ordinary or preference.

question_text: According to the course material, real markets are for physical or tangible assets such as plant, machinery, wheat, office, gold and buildings; intangible real assets include copyrights, patent and:
explanation: Intangible real assets include copyrights, patents and technical know-how.

question_text: According to the course material, financial markets trade on financial assets that promise future benefits in the form of cash payments such as bonds, certificates of deposit and:
explanation: Financial assets include bonds, CDs and treasury bills.

question_text: According to the course material, the important finance functions include long-term asset-mix or investment function, capital-mix or financing function, profit allocation or dividend function, and:
explanation: Four functions: investment, financing, dividend and liquidity.

question_text: According to the course material, investment decisions involve capital expenditures which are referred to as:
explanation: Investment decisions are capital budgeting decisions.

question_text: According to the course material, the mix of internal (equity) and external (debt) finance required by the enterprise is known as the:
option_a: capital structure of the business organization
explanation: Equity-debt mix is the capital structure.

question_text: According to the course material, the capital structure is said to be optimum when:
option_a: the market value of shares is maximized
explanation: Optimum capital structure maximises market value of shares.

question_text: According to the course material, the proportion of profits distributed as dividend is called the:
explanation: Dividend-payout ratio is the proportion of profits distributed as dividend.

question_text: According to the course material, the four main headings of risk that threaten postponed fruits of effort are physical, technical, economic and:
explanation: Risks: physical, technical, economic and political.

question_text: According to the course material, physical risks are risks that some accident may destroy or spoil some physical goods created by the work financed, for example a house may be destroyed by fire or:
option_a: a ship may be wrecked or sunk
option_b: only a GST unit may fail
option_d: only a labour union may fail
explanation: Physical risks include fire, flood, storm, theft, wrecked ships.

question_text: According to the course material, technical risks arise because the producer's skill or that of subordinates may not be up to the expected level, so the plan may:
option_a: fall short of achieving the intention
explanation: Technical risk is skill/process shortfall versus the plan.

question_text: According to the course material, economic risks remain even though the physical object created suffers no unexpected damage; they include the risk of an inadequate supply of resources and:
option_a: the risk of fall in demand for the product once it has been made
explanation: Economic risks include cost overruns/supply failure and demand fall.

question_text: According to the course material, political risks are risks of losses as the result of unforeseen intervention by:
explanation: Political risks come from unforeseen government intervention.

question_text: According to the course material, three ways of avoiding or reducing risk are additional expenditure on precautions, turning risks into regular costs by pooling them, and:
option_a: combining them with other risks operating in the opposite direction
explanation: Avoidance: extra precautions, pooling/insurance, offsetting opposite risks.

question_text: According to the course material, after reducing risks by precautions, insurance pooling or hedging, remaining risks must be borne by whoever provides the finance; partnership and limited liability company are two main institutional forms under which people join together sharing fully in:
explanation: Partnership and LLC share fully in both risks and profits.

question_text: According to the course material, the finance manager's duties include budgeting, raising funds, selecting and evaluating projects, and:
option_a: planning the marketing and pricing strategies
explanation: Duties include budgeting, funds, projects, and marketing/pricing strategies.

question_text: According to the course material, the treasurer oversees or manages the enterprise's liquid assets, liabilities, payroll and cashier activities, credits and collections, forecasting, capital budgeting and:
explanation: The treasurer covers liquidity, payroll, credit, forecasting, capital budgeting, investment and financing.

question_text: According to the course material, TMAs account for 30% of the total score and the end of course examination accounts for:
explanation: TMAs 30%; end-of-course examination 70%.

question_text: According to the course material, Anao (1993) defined finance as money affairs or money matters, implying all forms of money or near-money such as debt, cash, equity and:
explanation: Anao includes debt, cash, equity and certificates of deposits.
